validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Five of the seven findings reproduce at named lines I read directly in this pass. The two that do not reproduce are recorded as such rather than implemented: F3's cmdk console error does not exist in cmdk@1.1.1, and F1's process half is a property of this repo's config, not a defect fixable inside a ticket. The residual uncertainty is about intent, not code: F4 and F6 each offer two remedies and I picked one, with the alternative argued so a disagreeing reviewer has a defensible option in hand. This revision changes nothing technical from v1 — it corrects the destination channel for the control-run outputs in the four places the review named, so the implementer is never asked to edit the PR template that a checked-in project rule forbids touching.
validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #57 collects seven review findings against the command-bar e2e work landed in #48/#53. I re-checked all seven against the tree as it stands now and re-verified every line cited below in this pass; nothing has changed on main since v1 of this plan, so the technical plan stands unchanged. What changes in v2 is where the control-run evidence is recorded.

WHAT REPRODUCES. F2, F4, F5, F6 and F7 are still present exactly as described. packages/desktop-client/e2e/command-bar.test.ts:68 still declares `let settleMatch: () => void;` with no initialiser, assigned only inside the `new Promise` executor at :69-71 and called at :77 inside the `page.on('console')` listener, with `Promise.race([firstDialogWarning, page.waitForTimeout(CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS)])` at :88-91 and `expect(messages).toEqual([])` at :96. F2 is the same defect as the centre of the ticket in a second file: packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts:241 attaches a `page.on('pageerror')` listener and :266 reads the buffer, with only `toHaveURL` and two `toBeVisible()` calls between them — every one synchronises on the DOM, none on the CDP channel the errors arrive on. F6 is :102-104 (`toBeTruthy()` plus `not.toBe('Command Bar')`) against the English literals still pinned at :82 and :103. F7 is :9's `(dist/index.mjs:288 and :304)`.

WHAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE. F3 asserts a cmdk console error that does not exist. cmdk@1.1.1's published dist contains no console output, and 1.1.1 is what the lockfile resolves (yarn.lock pins `cmdk@npm:^1.1.1` to `version: 1.1.1`; packages/desktop-client/package.json:177 declares `^1.1.1`). Grepping the whole e2e tree for `key prop` and `Each child` returns nothing, so the false premise has no footprint in the repository at all: it lives only in the prose of the earlier work order and PR. There is no code to correct. I record the correction here so the next reviewer stops hunting for noise that cannot be generated, and I drop F3 rather than invent a change for it. F1 is half true: the drain really did ship with no execution evidence — `gh pr view 53` shows a body of six unchecked AC boxes and the pipeline footer, with no control output — but 'no automated stage can substitute for it' is a property of this repo's configuration, not a defect anyone can fix inside a ticket: .sdlc/config.yml:172 sets `verify.e2e: ""`, and .sdlc/config.yml is in forbidden_paths. What I can fix is the part that is mine: the drain's central claim was never checked by anything, so I make the test check it on every run.

THE ROOT CAUSE, AND WHY THIS IS ONE TICKET. Every one of these findings is the same bug class: a buffer filled by an out-of-band CDP channel is read after awaits that synchronise on something else entirely. There are exactly two such buffers in the e2e tree — `grep -rn "page.on('console'\|page.on('pageerror'" packages/desktop-client/e2e/` returns only command-bar.test.ts:72 and reports.test.ts:241, and `grep -rn 'toEqual(\[\])' packages/desktop-client/e2e/` returns only those files' two reads at :96 and :266 — so fixing one and not the other would leave the class half-fixed and make the two files disagree about the idiom. No production code changes: CommandBar.tsx:305 renders the Trans producing 'Search pages, accounts and reports' behind the hidden RadixDialog.Description the test guards, and nothing in this ticket touches it.

TWO DECISIONS THE REVIEW LEAVES OPEN. F4 asks for either a justification of the race or its removal; I remove it. The race shortens a failing run by about a second and never changes the verdict — on the passing path both arms of the race wait the full 1000ms, and on the failing path both report `expect(messages).toEqual([])` — and removing it deletes `settleMatch`, `firstDialogWarning` and the non-optional `let` in one go, which dissolves F5 structurally instead of answering it with a comment. F6 asks for either the literal back or all three English literals dropped together; I put the literal back, because the file is pinned to English regardless (lines 82 and 103, and Platform.isPlaywright empties availableLanguages so e2e always renders English), so the literal costs nothing it is not already paying and restores a content check that #39 had and #53 weakened. Dropping all three is a larger, separable change that would ship on its own.

WHAT IS NEW HERE. F1 is the review's sharpest point and it is not satisfied by asking for the same control run a second time — #48 asked, and it did not happen. So instead of a comment alone, the test gains a probe: it emits a message matching its own warning regex at the moment it begins draining, and polls until that message is in a buffer. If the channel stops delivering promptly, or the pattern stops matching Radix's real wording, the test goes red by itself on every run. That converts a claim nobody was checking into an assertion something checks, and re-proves the regex against the verbatim message each time instead of trusting prose that cites a third-party tarball. The probe must be emitted AFTER `expect(messages).toEqual([])` — it matches the same pattern, so run first it would poison the buffer it is meant to be independent of.

WHERE THE EVIDENCE GOES (the correction from v1's rejection). The control-run output does not go in the PR body. .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md, pulled in by CLAUDE.md as overriding default behaviour, says to create the PR with the unmodified template and never fill it in; and .sdlc/agents/implementer.md:76-79 says the implementer runs with a read-only token, cannot push or comment, and that anything destined for 'the PR body or in a comment' goes in implementer-reply.md at the repo root, which the pipeline posts on the pull request. So both control outputs are written into implementer-reply.md and reach the PR as a posted comment. This is the only channel available to the implementer, and the PR body is not one of them.

NO RELEASE NOTE. packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs runs from .github/workflows/sdlc-release.yml, which is workflow_dispatch-only and writes notes per PR at release time. The four most recent commits here, including the two most recent test-only ones, added no file under upcoming-release-notes/. This PR is test-only and adds none either.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Buffers filled by `page.on('console')` / `page.on('pageerror')` are delivered over CDP out of band, so every await between attaching the listener and reading the buffer must be one that waits on the DOM. Neither test does that: command-bar.test.ts works around it with an over-built race whose payload (`let settleMatch`, `Promise.race`) cannot be proven to be assigned before use and buys nothing, and reports.test.ts:241-266 does not work around it at all. Neither test proves its own drain can do its job, and #53 relaxed the description assertion without removing the English literals that made the relaxed form pointless.
validated_work_order.approach:
Two files, one idiom, no production code.

In command-bar.test.ts:
1. Doc comment: drop `(dist/index.mjs:288 and :304)`, keep the `@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15` pin and both verbatim messages, and say why the version but not the line numbers (F7).
2. Add a module-level `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` holding Radix's verbatim description-warning string.
3. Extract the listener into `watchDialogWarnings(page: Page): { messages: string[] }` next to `referredText`, so the test body and the probe share one filter and one type.
4. In the test body: delete `let settleMatch`, `firstDialogWarning` and the `Promise.race([...])`; call `await page.waitForTimeout(CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS)` directly. That is the whole synchronisation point, and it removes F5 with the code rather than around it (F4, F5).
5. Keep `expect(messages).toEqual([])` immediately after the drain — unchanged, and still first so the accessibility assertions below cannot mask it.
6. After that assertion, add the probe: attach a second `watchDialogWarnings`, `page.evaluate` a `console.warn` of `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` from inside the page, then `await expect.poll(() => [...probe.messages], { timeout: CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS }).toEqual([DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE])`. Poll, not a second fixed wait, so the cost on a healthy run is one round-trip and not another second (F1).
7. Restore `expect(await referredText(dialog, 'aria-describedby')).toBe('Search pages, accounts and reports')`, replacing `toBeTruthy()` and `not.toBe('Command Bar')` — the literal subsumes both, and the string is what CommandBar.tsx:305 renders through i18next's natural-language keys at lng: 'en' (F6).

In reports.test.ts: add a `PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS` constant and a comment naming the same CDP reason, then `await page.waitForTimeout(PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS)` immediately before `expect(pageErrors).toEqual([])` (F2). Same idiom as the sibling file, kept local to each file as the existing `CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS` already is, rather than hoisted into a shared helper for two callers with different channel names.

Finally, run both controls once and write both outputs — the failing run's output showing `expect(messages).toEqual([])` receiving the injected message, and the passing run's output with the drain line deleted — into implementer-reply.md at the repo root, along with a `git status` line confirming the tree is clean afterwards. Do not touch the PR body: .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md forbids filling in the PR template, and the implementer runs with a read-only token that cannot edit it in any case (.sdlc/agents/implementer.md:76-79). The pipeline posts implementer-reply.md on the pull request as a comment, which is where the evidence lands. The probe makes the first control self-checking from now on, but the second — that removing the drain makes the test pass — is a property of the drain's presence and is not something a test can assert about itself, so it still has to be run and written down. If the sandbox cannot start the dev server and the controls genuinely cannot be run, say exactly that in implementer-reply.md and name what was attempted; do not report an outcome that was not observed.

Add `const DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE = 'Warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}.'` beside `CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS`, documented as the verbatim string the probe emits so the pattern is re-proved against real wording each run. qa_script: Open $PREVIEW_URL, start a fresh budget with 'Don't use a server', then 'View demo'.
Open devtools and switch to the Console tab, keeping it visible.
Press ControlOrMeta+K and confirm the palette opens.
Confirm the console stayed clear of any Radix dialog accessibility warning for ~2 seconds after the open.
In the Elements panel select the role=dialog node and confirm aria-labelledby resolves to an element reading 'Command Bar'.
Confirm aria-describedby resolves to an element reading 'Search pages, accounts and reports' (not a dangling id, and not the same text as the title).
Press Escape and confirm the dialog detaches from the DOM.
Navigate to Reports, open a custom report in the empty budget, and confirm no uncaught page error appears in the console while the report loads.
Report whether any console error or warning appeared at any point; an uncaught page error or a Radix dialog warning is a failure even if the UI looks correct.
risks: The probe polls for up to CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS. On a heavily loaded machine CDP delivery could occasionally exceed that, producing a flake that fails loudly and correctly rather than passing vacuously — but it is a new flake surface. `expect.poll` defaults to 100ms intervals and returns as soon as the message lands, so the healthy-path cost is one round-trip, not a second.
Every run of the command-bar test now spends ~1s of unconditional wall clock that #39 did not. This is the price of the drain the review accepted; the race only ever hid it on green runs.

Restoring the description literal couples the test to an English string in production code. That coupling is pre-existing (lines 82 and 103, and Platform.isPlaywright empties availableLanguages), and i18n.ts uses natural-language keys with fallbackLng: false, so the English render is deterministic under e2e. If the production copy is reworded, this test fails — which is the intended signal, not a false positive.

The control runs may not be executable in the implementer's sandbox if the dev server cannot start. AC-6's how_to_verify says explicitly what to do in that case: record it under coverage_gaps rather than claim an outcome that was not observed. This is the same failure mode #48 had, so it is a live possibility rather than a theoretical one.

The implementer also does not write the PR body (forbidden by .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md) and does not commit implementer-reply.md.

validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The review's seven findings are not equally real, and the ticket's own instruction — check each one before planning it, drop what does not hold up — is what separates them. F2, F4, F5, F6 and F7 reproduce exactly as written and are small, precise edits. F3 does not reproduce at all: cmdk@1.1.1's published dist contains no console output and no e2e file references such an error, so the premise has no repository footprint to correct and I drop it rather than manufacture a change. F1 is half real: the missing execution evidence is genuine, but 'no automated stage can substitute for it' is a property of this repo's config, and .sdlc/config.yml is forbidden to this ticket — so the remedy has to be something the test does itself. Hence the probe, which turns the drain's unverified claim into an assertion that fails when the channel misbehaves, rather than a control run nobody repeats.

The two open decisions were where the review offered a choice. F4 could be answered by justifying the race or by removing it; removal also deletes the non-optional `let settleMatch`, so it resolves F5 structurally instead of by comment. F6 could be answered by restoring the description literal or by dropping all three English literals; restoring is cheaper, loses nothing, and the English render is deterministic in e2e anyway, while the locale-independent version would ship on its own. Both picks are argued above and both alternatives are recorded in alternatives_considered so a disagreeing reviewer does not have to reconstruct them.

The plan review rejected v1 on a single point, and it was a point about channels rather than about code. AC-6, AC-7's fallback, and the closing paragraph of approach all required the control-run outputs in the PR body — a destination the implementer cannot reach (read-only token, no push) and is forbidden from writing (the project rule against filling in the PR template). Because QA is held to the acceptance array id by id, that would have failed a change that did exactly what the repo rules require, on the criterion intended to close the ticket's central finding. This revision changes nothing about the implementation: implementer-reply.md at the repo root is the implementer's only output channel, the pipeline already posts it on the pull request as a comment, and AC-6 now names that comment and states explicitly that an unmodified PR template body is the correct outcome rather than a failure. The alternative — keeping the PR body and asking the implementer to override a checked-in project rule — is recorded in alternatives_considered so the rejection is not re-litigated.

One constraint shaped every acceptance criterion: nothing in CI typechecks or runs these files (packages/desktop-client/tsconfig.json excludes e2e, verify.e2e is empty, vitest's include skips the directory). Criteria about the test files' own logic are therefore verify: test with the exact command named, and only the app behaviour both tests guard is verify: browser. Writing a browser-observable criterion for a test refactor would have been theatre.
